title: Arkret Realm Policy-Server Self-Management Operation DTOs
description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Realm policy-server config operations (ak.self.realm_policy_server.*). PUT carries the caller-signed durable ak.realm.policy_server Move; DELETE carries the same kind with payload {tombstone:true}. Both MUST carry head_eq for the complete settled value when the direct cell already holds one, and the caller attaches that precondition because it is inside the bytes it signs. An existing tombstone is an idempotent empty success, while a never-written or inherited-only direct cell returns not_found. Both mutation operations require ak.policy.manage; see spec/v1/zh/authz/policy-server.md §2.

from_org_fallback.description: True when the config was resolved via the governed_by / org-fallback chain rather than a row on the Realm itself.

realm_policy_server_event_submission.description: Shared submission shape for both policy-server writes. Replace and delete write the same CAS-register cell with the same Event kind, so they share one submission def and differ only in whether the payload is a declaration or the value tombstone. These operations used to take the declaration fields directly, which left the signature for the service to add -- exactly what capabilities.md sections 118/361 and key-management.md section 411 forbid. The Realm is single-sourced by event.realm_id and MUST equal the path realm_id. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event; admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller and that the caller holds ak.policy.manage. When the direct cell already holds a settled declaration or tombstone, the Event MUST carry a head_eq precondition on ak:cell:ak.component.realm.policy_server.v1:null naming that complete value; the caller attaches it because preconditions are inside the signed bytes, so a concurrent write makes the later submission fail its precondition rather than silently clobbering the cell.

realm_policy_server_replace_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.policy_server declaration Move and nothing else. The whole declaration is policy_server_event.event.payload (realm_policy_server_declaration_payload), which is the durable value the reducer stores -- there is no narrower REST projection of it left to drift.

policy_server_event.description: Closed ak.realm.policy_server Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, whose payload is a declaration.

realm_policy_server_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed value-tombstone ak.realm.policy_server Move and nothing else. The payload is exactly {"tombstone":true}. This is a DELETE with a request body -- the same shape ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete already uses -- because the durable removal is a signed Event and no signature fits in a bodyless request.

policy_server_event.description: Closed ak.realm.policy_server Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, with payload pinned to the value tombstone.
